sentence_stem: Because the shop was closed on Sunday,
correct_completion: we bought our bread on Saturday.
full_sentence: Because the shop was closed on Sunday, we bought our bread on Saturday.
acceptable_variants: we had to buy our bread on Saturday.
we went to another bakery that day.

options.why_wrong: 'Although' signals contrast, while 'because' signals cause; the two connectors cannot both introduce the same clause.

options.text: so we bought bread on Sunday.
options.why_wrong: This combines 'because' with 'so' in one clause and contradicts the fact that the shop was closed on Sunday.

options.text: we bought our bread on Saturday.
the shop was open on Monday.
options.why_wrong: This gives a fact about a different day and does not show the result of the shop being closed on Sunday.

explanation: After 'because', we need a main clause that shows the result of the shop being closed. Learners should avoid combining 'because' with another connector such as 'although' or 'so' in the same sentence.
